title: The Locker of Lake Minnow
premise: Hazel Dravenmoor, the only out kid in the dying fishing town of Lake Minnow, counts the days until graduation while hiding in plain sight. When her best friend and secret crush, Juniper Vale, vanishes and leaves behind a set of locker keys, Hazel discovers Juniper was competing for a music conservatory scholarship that could have been their shared escape — and that Juniper's disappearance is tangled in her family's debt to Hazel's own grandmother. To find her, Hazel must enter and win the town's absurd annual ice-fishing championship, where the real prize isn't the trophy but access to the Vale family's frozen-over boathouse and the truth inside it. In the climax, Hazel wins the championship, confronts her grandmother, and finds Juniper hiding in the boathouse after faking her disappearance to escape an arranged conservatory audition rigged by her parents; the two girls perform the audition piece together, choosing love over duty and claiming an identity neither had to hide.
about_author: E. M. Fairweather grew up in a lakeside town smaller than the one in this book and has been writing about the kids who stay and the kids who leave ever since. A former debate coach and amateur ice fisher, Fairweather lives with a very old cat and a very new canoe.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred and Me
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She maps the social geography of Lake Minnow High — where she sits, who looks away, how many days until graduation. Establishes her invisibility as armor and her longing for Juniper Vale, her only friend. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as patience.

chapters.title: The Keys in the Snow
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Juniper misses their morning ritual, then a week of school. Hazel finds a plastic bag taped under their shared bench by the dock: Juniper's locker keys and a note reading 'Don't let them win the lake.' Emotional beat: fear cracking open routine.

chapters.title: Locker 114
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Using the keys, she opens Juniper's locker and finds sheet music, a conservatory brochure, and a photo of the two of them with the words 'both of us or neither' scrawled on the back. Emotional beat: the first hint that Juniper's secrets included Hazel herself.

chapters.title: The Vale Family Silence
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She visits the Vale house; Juniper's parents are cold, insist she's 'away at auditions,' and their eyes go to the frozen lake when they say it. Hazel notices a padlocked boathouse. Emotional beat: the town's politeness as a wall.

chapters.title: What Grandma Keeps in the Den
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Searching her grandmother's study for lake records, Hazel finds a decades-old ledger: the Vales owe the Dravenmoors a debt tied to the boathouse, and her grandmother holds the only key. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as leverage.

chapters.title: The Championship Nobody Cares About
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The annual Ice Classic is announced; the winner receives 'honorary access' to all lakeside properties for the year — including, Hazel realizes, the boathouse. She signs up on impulse. Emotional beat: reckless hope.

chapters.title: Learning to Fish in Public
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, with a flashback in Juniper's voice via found cassette tapes. Hazel trains with gruff retired fisherman Walt Okafor, who knew her late father and sees through her. Emotional beat: being seen without flinching, for the first time.

chapters.title: Tape One: 'If You're Listening'
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV (cassette recording). Juniper explains her parents' plan: a rigged audition to send her to a conservatory that will 'fix' her, and her discovery that the boathouse holds proof of what her family traded away. Emotional beat: terror and love braided together.

chapters.title: Rivals on the Ice
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Qualifying round: she faces Dale Pruitt, the sheriff's son who has bullied her for years, and wins narrowly by reading the ice better. The town notices her for the first time. Emotional beat: visibility as both threat and power.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Other Name
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She deciphers more of the ledger: her own father co-signed the Vale debt before his death, meaning Hazel inherited both sides of the bargain. Her grandmother catches her reading it. Emotional beat: family as a trap with her name on it.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Terms
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Her grandmother offers a deal: win the championship, hand over whatever's in the boathouse, and Hazel's future is 'secured' — college paid, debts cleared, provided she drops the search for Juniper. Emotional beat: love offered as a cage.

chapters.title: Tape Two: 'The Boathouse'
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV (recording). Juniper describes finding documents proving her parents falsified the debt to control her future, and her plan to hide until the audition date to expose them. She says Hazel's name at the end. Emotional beat: a confession meant only for Hazel.

chapters.title: Dale Knows Something
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Dale Pruitt, oddly subdued, warns Hazel off the lake at night — then lets slip he saw someone near the boathouse weeks ago. His bullying, it emerges, was cover for his own secret. Emotional beat: enemies revealed as fellow prisoners.

chapters.title: Night on the Ice
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel and Dale cross the frozen lake after dark; the ice groans, they nearly go through, and she sees light moving inside the padlocked boathouse. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into certainty that Juniper is alive.

chapters.title: Semifinals and a Grandmother's Watch
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel advances to the semifinal while her grandmother watches with new intensity, clearly aware of the night crossing. Walt tells Hazel what her father was really like — a man who also chose duty over love, and regretted it. Emotional beat: inheritance as warning.

chapters.title: The Rigged Audition
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She learns from a conservatory letter in Juniper's locker that the audition panel includes her own grandmother — the scholarship was designed to separate the girls all along. Emotional beat: the full machinery of the trap revealed.

chapters.title: Tape Three: 'Both of Us or Neither'
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV (recording). Juniper admits she left the keys because she couldn't leave without Hazel knowing, couldn't ask her to come, and couldn't go alone. She plays the audition piece — a duet arranged for two. Emotional beat: love stated plainly at last.

chapters.title: The Final
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Championship day: the whole town on the ice. Hazel wins the Ice Classic in a tense duel with Dale, who throws the last hole to her with a nod. She is handed honorary access to every lakeside property — including the boathouse key. Emotional beat: triumph that feels like a beginning.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Opens
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Inside the boathouse: Juniper, alive, thin, defiant — and the documents proving her parents' and grandmother's scheme. The reunion is angry, tearful, and true. Emotional beat: relief colliding with betrayal's aftershocks.

chapters.title: The Audition Room
chapters.summary: Alternating Hazel and Juniper POV. The girls walk into the audition together and perform the duet as written for two, refusing to be separated, while the panel — including Hazel's grandmother — realizes the plan has failed. Emotional beat: love against duty, played out loud.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says Now
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Confrontation with her grandmother: Hazel tears up the debt page, choosing neither inheritance nor escape but a third thing — truth. Her grandmother, shaken, sees her late son in Hazel's defiance. Emotional beat: breaking a chain without hating the hand that forged it.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Spring: both girls accepted to the conservatory on their own merits; the town adjusts, imperfectly, to two girls walking to school holding hands. Hazel stops counting days. Emotional beat: identity claimed, home redefined, the future unlocked.
